latest_release.body:
The PC app on Linux and on Windows on ARM, Phone as microphone, Play on phone, your phone's sound on the PC, a Nightly channel, and the fixes for what people reported since 0.1.4.

### Downloads

| Download | For | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| [Nectarlink-0.1.5-x64-setup.exe](https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/releases/download/v0.1.5/Nectarlink-0.1.5-x64-setup.exe) | Windows | Windows 10 (2004+) or 11, 64-bit Intel or AMD (Phone as webcam needs Windows 11) |
| [Nectarlink-0.1.5-arm64-setup.exe](https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/releases/download/v0.1.5/Nectarlink-0.1.5-arm64-setup.exe) | Windows on ARM | Windows 11 on ARM (Snapdragon) |
| [nectarlink_0.1.5_amd64.deb](https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/releases/download/v0.1.5/nectarlink_0.1.5_amd64.deb) | Ubuntu, Debian | Ubuntu 24.04 or newer, Debian 13, 64-bit Intel or AMD |
| [nectarlink-0.1.5-1.x86_64.rpm](https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/releases/download/v0.1.5/nectarlink-0.1.5-1.x86_64.rpm) | Fedora, openSUSE | Fedora 40 or newer, 64-bit Intel or AMD |
| [Nectarlink-0.1.5-x86_64.AppImage](https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/releases/download/v0.1.5/Nectarlink-0.1.5-x86_64.AppImage) | Other Linux | A distribution from 2024 or newer, 64-bit Intel or AMD |
| [Nectarlink-0.1.5-linux-x86_64.tar.gz](https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/releases/download/v0.1.5/Nectarlink-0.1.5-linux-x86_64.tar.gz) | Other Linux | As the AppImage |
| [Nectarlink-0.1.5-android.apk](https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/releases/download/v0.1.5/Nectarlink-0.1.5-android.apk) | Android | Android 8.0 or newer |

All are listed with their SHA-256 hashes in [SHA256SUMS.txt](https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/releases/download/v0.1.5/SHA256SUMS.txt). On Linux, `curl -fsSL https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh` picks the right one. Installed copies update themselves.

### New

- **Nix flake.** `nix run` starts the PC app on Linux, and `nix develop` gives a development shell. Thanks to [@m-uvex](https://github.com/m-uvex) ([#173](https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/pull/173)).
- **Delete photos from the PC.** Select them on the Photos page and they go to the phone's trash, where you can still restore them. It needs All files access on the phone ([#174](https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/issues/174)).
- **SD cards in File Explorer.** With All files access, an SD card or USB drive in the phone shows as a folder of its own (such as **SD card**) beside the internal storage's folders. Before Android 11, Android lets apps only read SD cards ([D#149](https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/discussions/149)).
- **Turkish.** The Android and PC apps speak Turkish (Türkçe): pick it in Settings, or they follow the system's language. Thanks to [@sedatdagg](https://github.com/sedatdagg).
- **Your phone's sound on the PC, without mirroring.** **Phone sound on this PC** on Home plays what the phone plays through the PC's speakers or headphones, with no mirror window. With Elevated it starts right away; otherwise the phone asks once, as for mirroring. The phone goes quiet meanwhile and its media volume comes back after ([#94](https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/issues/94)).
- **Sharing your PC's screen with the phone uses H.265** when both sides can, and H.264 otherwise. Thanks to [@AS8148](https://github.com/AS8148) ([#66](https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/pull/66)).
- **Hardware video for screen sharing on Linux.** With FFmpeg 6 to 9 installed, sharing the PC's screen and showing a shared screen use the GPU (VAAPI, NVIDIA or Intel QSV) and fall back to software H.264 when it can't. Thanks to [@AS8148](https://github.com/AS8148) ([#67](https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/pull/67)).
- **Elevated over USB.** Plug the phone into the PC with USB debugging allowed and Elevated starts by itself, without setting up Wireless debugging. It runs while the cable is in, and needs Android's `adb` running on the PC (Google's platform-tools, then `adb start-server`). The PC only

detail.readme:
# NectarLink **Your Android phone and your PC, working as one.** Notifications, messages, calls, clipboard, files, photos, screen mirroring and phone apps in windows, between Android and Windows 10 (2004+), Windows 11 or Linux. Free and open source. Local-first, end-to-end encrypted, no account and no cloud. Hi, I'm Bee, and yes, a bee built an app called NectarLink. I build cool stuff in the open on [𝕏 @thtbee_](https://x.com/thtbee_), so come see what's next. Feedback, bugs or ideas? DM me directly. [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/thtbee/nectarlink?label=download)](https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/releases/latest) [![CI](https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Apps: GPL-3.0-or-later](https://img.shields.io/badge/apps-GPL--3.0--or--later-blue)](LICENSE) [![Core: MPL-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/core-MPL--2.0-blue)](LICENSE)

## Why NectarLink NectarLink came out of my own frustration. I kept juggling Phone Link for notifications and messages, KDE Connect for the clipboard and LocalSend for files, and always wanted one app that did all of it. So I made one. It covers what those three did for me, with one app on each side, plus a lot of new features I wanted that I think you'll enjoy having too. ## Download | | Download | Needs | |---|---|---| | **Windows (x64)** | [Installer (.exe)](https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/releases/download/v0.1.5/Nectarlink-0.1.5-x64-setup.exe) | Windows 10 (2004+) or 11, 64-bit Intel or AMD (Phone as webcam needs Windows 11) | | **Windows (ARM64)** | [Installer (.exe)](https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/releases/download/v0.1.5/Nectarlink-0.1.5-arm64-setup.exe) | Windows 11 on ARM (Snapdragon) | | **Linux (x86_64)** | [One command](#on-linux), or a [.deb](https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/releases/download/v0.1.5/nectarlink_0.1.5_amd64.deb), [.rpm](https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/releases/download/v0.1.5/nectarlink-0.1.5-1.x86_64.rpm), [AppImage](https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/releases/download/v0.1.5/Nectarlink-0.1.5-x86_64.AppImage) or [.tar.gz](https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/releases/download/v0.1.5/Nectarlink-0.1.5-linux-x86_64.tar.gz) | Ubuntu 24.04 or newer, Debian 13, Fedora 40 or newer, 64-bit Intel or AMD | | **Android** | [App (.apk)](https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/releases/download/v0.1.5/Nectarlink-0.1.5-android.apk) | Android 8.0 or newer | The apps update themselves from GitHub Releases and check every download against its SHA-256 sums. ### On Linux One command installs NectarLink with everything it needs, and shows each step as it goes: ```bash curl -fsSL https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh ``` It picks the package for your system (.deb with apt, .rpm with dnf or zypper, the tarball elsewhere), checks it against the release's SHA-256 sums and installs it with its dependencies. Then it sets up the phone as a webcam, the phone as a keyboard and mouse, and the firewall for your local network only. To remove it all again, end the same command with `sh -s -- --uninstall` instead of `sh`. See [Installing on Linux](docs/guide/getting-started.md#on-linux) for the details. > [!NOTE] > SmartScreen may warn about the Windows installer the first time, because it > isn't code-signed yet: choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**. On Android, > allow your browser or file manager to install apps when asked. > [!IMPORTANT] > In India and many other countries, Google Play Protect blocks the APK with > no **Install anyway** button. Pause **Scan apps with Play Protect** while you > install it (Play Store › your profile › Play Protect › Settings), then turn it > back on, or install it from a PC with `adb install`. See > [Play Protect blocks the APK](docs/guide/troubleshooting.md#google-play-protect-blocks-the-apk-without-an-install-anyway-button). ## Get started 1. Install NectarLink on your PC and on your phone. 2. On the PC, the setup walkthrough shows a QR code. Scan it with the phone (from the NectarLink app or any camera app), or pick the PC from the phone's list of nearby devices and compare a 6-digit code. A USB cable works too, with Android's `adb` running on the PC. 3. Allow what you want to share. Every feature has its own switch per device, and the sensitive ones are off until you turn them on. 4. Optional: set up **Wireless debugging** once in the phone app for the features Android reserves for privileged apps (phone apps in windows, real touch input, background clipboard sync). No root, nothing else to install. The [user guide](docs/guide/README.md) walks through every step and feature. ## What it does **Stay on top of your phone** - **Notifications** on the PC, with replies, actions, Live Updates (progress, timers, deliveries) and a **Copy code** button for one-time codes. Clear on one side, cleared on the other. - **Messages**: SMS and MMS conversations plus chats from RCS, WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal and other apps in one inbox. Reply, send pictures, start new conversations. - **Calls**: see who's calling, answer, decline or hang up from the PC, call any number or contact through the phone, and browse recent calls. **Move things between devices** - **Clipboard**: copy on one device, paste on the other, with optional encrypted history. Passwords from password managers are never sent, and one-time codes are never kept in the history. - **Files and folders** both ways at Wi-Fi speed, with resume after a dropped connection, **Send to** in File Explorer, and the phone's storage in File Explorer. It also works with LocalSend devices, without pairing. - **Synced folders**: keep a phone folder and a PC folder in step, one way or both ways, with a copy kept when a file changed on both sides. - **Photos**: the phone's camera roll, screenshots and albums on the PC, and **Photo backup**, which copies new photos into a folder on the PC by year and month and never deletes anything. - **Handoff**: links, maps and videos (at the same timestamp) open on the other device. **Use your phone from the PC** - **Screen mirroring** at up to 60 frames a second with the phone's sound, screenshots and recording. - **Apps**: open any phone app in a window of its own on the PC, with its own taskbar icon, running beside whatever the phone shows. - **Type on the phone** with the PC keyboard, without mirroring. - **Phone controls** on the PC: Do Not Disturb, ringer, volume, flashlight, brightness, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. **Use your PC from the phone** - **Touchpad, air mouse, keyboard, voice typing and presentation remote.** - **Your PC's screen on the phone**, with control from the phone. - **Deck**: a Stream Deck style grid of buttons for the PC (media, shortcuts, apps, OBS Studio, commands), with live volume and mute. - **Lock, sleep and wake** the PC. **Camera and sound** - **Phone as a webcam** in Zoom, Teams, Meet, OBS and the Camera app. - **Continuity Camera**: take a photo or scan a document with the phone and have it on the PC's clipboard. - **Phone as a speaker** for the PC's sound, and a **voice recorder** that saves straight to the PC. - **The phone's sound on the PC**, without a mirror window. - **Phone as a microphone** for Discord, Zoom, OBS or Teams, through a virtual audio cable such as VB-CABLE. - **Play on phone**: carry on with the video playing on the PC. **And more**: media controls both ways, battery alerts, Find my device, a searchable **Timeline** of everything that moved, a **Command Palette** (`Ctrl+Alt+Space`), a slide-out **Shelf**, a home-screen widget, and a **Connection Doctor** that finds and fixes what keeps devices from connecting. An optional **Nectar Island** at the top of the screen shows calls, music and transfers. Four themes, **Hive**, **Bloom**, **Glass** and **Graphite**, each in light and dark. In English, German, Turkish, Simplified Chinese, Brazilian Portuguese, Vietnamese and Spanish. ### Platform support | Feature | Windows | Linux | macOS (Preview) | |---|---|---|---| | Pairing & mutual TLS | Yes | Yes | Yes | | Files & folder transfer | Yes | Yes | Yes | | Photos browser & download | Yes | Yes | Yes | | Continuity Camera | Yes | Yes | Yes | | Calls & SMS viewer | Yes | Yes | Yes | | Phone quick toggles & volume | Yes | Yes | Yes | | Clipboard text & image sync | Yes | Yes | Yes (two-way text, incoming photo) | | System notifications | Yes | Yes | Yes (system banners) | | Phone screen mirroring | Yes | Yes | Not yet (in development) | | Screen recording (MP4) | Yes | Yes | Not yet | | PC audio stream / phone mic | Yes | Yes | Not yet | | Phone as webcam | Yes | Yes (with v4l2loopback) | Not yet | | Phone storage in the file manager | Yes | Yes | Not yet | ## Private by design - **Local-first.** Devices talk directly over your network, a USB cable or Tailscale. Nothing goes through a server, and there's no account. - **End-to-end encrypted.** Every connection is QUIC with TLS 1.3, authenticated with device keys exchanged when you pair. Keys are protected by Windows DPAPI, the macOS Keychain and the Android Keystore. On Linux, for now, only by file permissions. - **You decide what's shared.** Each paired device has its own feature switches. Remote control of the PC, shell commands and phone storage are off until you allow them. - **The only internet traffic** is the update check against GitHub (which you can turn off), and, if you turn it on, **Connect over mobile data**, which relays encrypted traffic it can't read. Voice typing uses your phone's own speech recognizer, which may use its provider's servers. Details: [Privacy and security](docs/guide/privacy-and-security.md) and the [security model](docs/technical/security-model.md). ## Screenshots **Hive** is an exclusive theme: honey, with a living honeycomb that breathes behind the app. | Hive, light | Hive, dark | |:---:|:---:| | | | Also **Bloom**, soft and colorful; **Glass**, translucent cards over the Windows backdrop; and **Graphite**, ink on paper. All in light and dark. | Bloom | Glass | Graphite | |:---:|:---:|:---:| | | | | | | | |

## How it works ``` Android app (Kotlin, Compose) Desktop app (Qt Quick, Rust) │ UniFFI │ cxx-qt ▼ ▼ ┌─────────────────────┐ QUIC (iroh), ┌─────────────────────┐ │ nectarlink-core │◄────────────────►│ nectarlink-core │ │ pairing, sessions, │ end-to-end │ pairing, sessions, │ │ storage, features │ encrypted │ storage, features │ └─────────────────────┘ └─────────────────────┘ ``` - **One core, two apps.** Protocol, pairing, sessions, the trust store and the capability matrix live in Rust (`core/`) and run unchanged on both platforms. - **Native on both sides.** A desktop app for Windows and Linux built with Qt Quick and Rust, and an Android app built with Jetpack Compose. - **Capability matrix.** Both apps work out which features a pair of devices supports and what would enable the rest, so the interface never offers something that can't work. - **Protocol.** Versioned and documented in [docs/protocol/v0.md](docs/protocol/v0.md): length-prefixed CBOR messages on QUIC streams. ## Repository layout ``` core/ nectarlink-protocol/ Message types, framing, pairing cryptography (MPL-2.0) nectarlink-core/ Identity, trust store, pairing, sessions, features (MPL-2.0) nectarlink-ffi/ UniFFI bindings used by the Android app (MPL-2.0) nectarlink-adb/ Client for the PC's adb, for USB connections (MPL-2.0) nectarlink-cli/ Command-line client (`nectarlink`) (GPL) desktop/ app/ Desktop app: Rust host, cxx-qt bridge, QML UI (GPL) vcam/ Windows 11 virtual camera Media Foundation DLL (GPL) installer/ NSIS installer script and Sparse Package manifest (GPL) packaging/ Linux packages and the install script (GPL) android/ Android app: Kotlin and Jetpack Compose (API 26+) (GPL) assets/fonts/ Fonts both apps ship with (OFL-1.1) assets/brand/ The app icon (see the trademark policy) tools/xtask/ Code generation (theme tokens) and checks (GPL) third_party/ Patched copies of dependencies, under their own licenses spikes/ Technical experiments with their results scripts/ Build, packaging and check scripts docs/ Guide, technical docs, protocol, design system (CC BY 4.0) ``` ## Building from source | Part | Needs | |---|---| | Core and CLI | [Rust](https://rustup.rs) (stable, pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml`) | | Windows app | Windows 11, Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools (C++), [Qt 6.12](https://www.qt.io/download-open-source) for MSVC 2022 x64 | | Linux app | Ubuntu 24.04 or newer (glibc 2.39), a C++17 compiler, pkg-config, the X11, Wayland and D-Bus development packages, [Qt 6.12](https://www.qt.io/download-open-source) (`gcc_64`, with Qt Shader Tools and Qt Wayland Compositor) | | macOS app | macOS 14+, Xcode Command Line Tools, [Qt 6.12](https://www.qt.io/download-open-source) (or Homebrew Qt 6) | | Android app | Android SDK (platform 37, NDK 30.0.16248370), JDK 17 or newer, `cargo-ndk` (see [android/README.md](android/README.md)) | For Linux hardware video encoding and decoding, install `libavcodec-dev` and `libavutil-dev` before building. The backend loads the matching FFmpeg runtime libraries when needed and tries available GPU drivers. Release packages support FFmpeg 6 through 9: the Ubuntu 24.04 release build includes an FFmpeg 6 backend, and separate adapters support versions 7, 8 and 9. Source builds use the matching runtime for their headers. Without matching libraries or a working hardware backend, the existing software H.264 path remains available. HEVC encoding requires hardware; if unavailable, screen sharing falls back to H.264. ```sh cargo test -p nectarlink-protocol -p nectarlink-core -p nectarlink-ffi # core and tests cargo run -p nectarlink-cli -- --help # command-line client cargo run -p nectarlink-desktop # desktop app (Qt's bin on PATH) cd android && ./gradlew assembleDebug # Android app ``` ```powershell ./scripts/package.ps1 # Windows installer: target\package\Nectarlink--x64-setup.exe ./scripts/check.ps1 # every check CI runs; add -Android and -Arm64 for the full set ``` Releases are built by CI from a `v*` tag; see [docs/technical/releasing.md](docs/technical/releasing.md). ### With Nix Run or develop NectarLink using Nix flakes: ```sh nix run # run desktop app nix run .#cli # run CLI client nix develop # enter development environment ``` ## Documentation - [User guide](docs/guide/README.md): setup, pairing and every feature, on Windows, Linux and Android - [Technical documentation](docs/technical/README.md): architecture, security model, protocol, storage, performance and builds - [Protocol v0](docs/protocol/v0.md) and the [capability registry](docs/protocol/capabilities.md) - [Architecture decision records](docs/adr) and the [design system](docs/design/README.md) - [Project plan and roadmap](docs/PLAN.md) ## Questions and ideas Ask questions, share ideas and show your setup in [Discussions](https://github.com/thtbee/nectarlink/discussions). Issues are for bugs and agreed feature work. ## Contributing Contributions are welcome. Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) first; for anything larger than a small fix, open an issue to agree on the approach. Contributions are accepted under the [Developer Certificate of Origin](DCO.txt), and everyone is expected to follow the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). To translate NectarLink into your language, see [docs/translating.md](docs/translating.md). To report a security issue, follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). Please don't open a public issue. ## License - Desktop and Android apps, CLI: [GPL-3.0-or-later](LICENSES/GPL-3.0-or-later.txt), with an [app-store exception](LICENSES/APP-STORE-EXCEPTION.md) - Core libraries: [MPL-2.0](LICENSES/MPL-2.0.txt) - Protocol specification and documentation: [CC BY 4.0](LICENSES/CC-BY-4.0.txt) See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for which license applies where. The NectarLink name and logo are covered by the [trademark policy](TRADEMARKS.md).
